description: Name the bright star, planet or Moon closest to a direction (azimuth, elevation) at a place and time, within 15 degrees. Use it for a steady point of light; for something that moved use what_did_i_see, for a precise satellite match use identify. Bright objects only (about magnitude 1.5 or brighter); refraction near the horizon is not modelled.

az.description: Direction in degrees from true north, clockwise: 0 = north, 90 = east, 180 = south, 270 = west.

el.description: Height above the horizon in degrees: 0 = horizon, 90 = straight overhead.

lang.description: Language of the text fields: fr (default) or en.

lat.description: Observer latitude in decimal degrees, WGS84 (north positive).

lng.description: Observer longitude in decimal degrees, WGS84 (east positive). lon and lng are aliases: give one.

lon.description: Observer longitude in decimal degrees, WGS84 (east positive). lon and lng are aliases: give one.

time.description: Moment of the observation, ISO-8601 (default now).

name: which_star

outputSchema.description: Returns best {name, kind, az, el, separation_deg}, others [...], asked, note.

title: Name a star or planet
